BiblicalUsage: Jerusalem gives gifts to all her lovers, hiring them to come to her from every side, and the LORD names the payment for what it is.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the verse strips the romance from idolatry: the harlot pays her lovers instead of being paid, and the city that chased other gods ends up buying what it once was given freely.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
